subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: The Hand
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Hand usable.

hook.text: Handprints on cave walls are 40,000 years old. Someone pressed paint to stone and said: I exist.

buildup.text: Hands create, destroy, heal, and bless. The Hamsa hand in the Middle East wards off evil.

discovery.text: In Buddhism, hand positions—mudras—convey full teachings. The angle of fingers carries meaning.

twist.text: A raised hand means stop. A clenched fist means resistance. Same body part, opposite meanings.

climax.text: The hand is the body's most expressive tool. Myths encoded its gestures with sacred weight.

punchline.text: Open or closed, it always says something.

quiz.question: What are mudras in Buddhist practice?
